**Finding submitted: deviation (IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data).**

- **What the document does:** Article III (p0048) gives Licensor all right, title and interest in the Licensed Technology and all Intellectual Property Rights therein; the defined term "INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS" (1.6) covers only Licensor's rights, and "DERIVATIVE WORK" (1.3) sweeps in all additions, modifications and enhancements. Combined with Article VII(b) (p0087), the bespoke client front end and enhancements we pay for become Licensor-owned Platform Software, and our only right is a non-exclusive, Field-of-Use-limited licence that terminates with the Agreement (Article XXI).
- **Why it fails the fallback:** no ownership of funded deliverables and no perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence back; and the Agreement contains no reservation of our rights in the trade, order and client data we transmit. Vendor's retention of its platform is fine and is not challenged.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** a carve-out inserted after Article III confirming we retain all Licensee Data and our IP, assigning customization deliverables we fund to us (Licensor keeping pre-existing platform IP plus a perpetual licence back to embedded Licensor IP), and barring joint ownership.
